programmes.name_local: Bank of Industry (BOI) SME and youth entrepreneurship financing
programmes.name_en: Bank of Industry (BOI) SME and youth entrepreneurship financing
programmes.amount_note: BOI lends to Nigerian enterprises across many products, typically from NGN 1 million (Youth Entrepreneurship Support and SME tiers) up to hundreds of millions or more for industrial projects, at single-digit to low-double-digit interest rates depending on the fund.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling applications through the BOI customer portal; individual on-lending funds open and close as their allocations are drawn down.

procedure_steps.detail: Register on the BOI customer portal and select the relevant product.
Submit the business plan, financials and collateral or guarantee details.
Offer letter, perfection of security and disbursement.

eligibility.other_note: Nigerian registered enterprises. Most BOI products require a bank guarantee or acceptable collateral, which is the main barrier for early-stage startups.

programmes.name_local: NITDA / National Information Technology Development Fund startup and innovation support
programmes.name_en: NITDA / National Information Technology Development Fund startup and innovation support
programmes.funder: National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA), Nigeria
programmes.amount_note: NITDA supports Nigerian technology startups through its innovation hubs (including the Office for Nigerian Digital Innovation), incubation, capacity-building grants and challenge funds. Individual award sizes are set per programme and are not published as a standing figure.
programmes.deadline_note: NITDA runs discrete programmes and challenges rather than a standing grant window; opportunities are announced on nitda.gov.ng and through ONDI.
programmes.reopen_note: NITDA's startup support is delivered through rotating initiatives (for example the Nigeria Startup Act implementation, ONDI's Startup Support and Engagement Portal, and periodic innovation challenges). Register on the Nigeria Startup Portal to be notified.

procedure_steps.detail: Register on the Nigeria Startup Portal / ONDI platform.
Apply to the specific open programme or challenge.
Support delivered as grants, incubation or in-kind services.

programmes.name_local: Nigeria Startup Act - startup labelling and incentives
programmes.name_en: Nigeria Startup Act - startup labelling and incentives
programmes.funder: National Council for Digital Innovation and Entrepreneurship / NITDA, Nigeria
programmes.amount_note: Labelled startups qualify for a package of incentives rather than a cash grant: pioneer status tax relief for up to four years, tax credits on qualifying R&D and staff training, relief on capital gains for investors, and access to the Startup Investment Seed Fund administered through the Nigeria Sovereign Investment Authority.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling applications for the startup label through the Startup Support and Engagement Portal.

procedure_steps.detail: Register the company on the Nigeria Startup Portal.
Apply for the startup label with evidence of innovation and eligibility.
Apply the incentives through the relevant tax and regulatory bodies.

documents_required.doc: CAC incorporation certificate (company under 10 years old)

eligibility.other_note: Company must be registered in Nigeria, less than 10 years old, with at least one Nigerian founder or co-founder, and its objects must involve creation, innovation, production or distribution of a digital technology product or process.

programmes.amount_note: US$5,000 non-refundable seed capital plus a 12-week training programme and mentorship
programmes.deadline_note: Applications open on 1 January each year and close on 31 March, via the TEFConnect platform
programmes.reopen_note: Opens every 1 January and closes 31 March. Register on TEFConnect ahead of the window.

eligibility.other_note: African-based businesses in operation for no more than three years. Applicants must be resident in an African country.
